2026-11-19.caption:
A clean, correct claim can still be worth nothing if it goes out too late.

Medicare: 12 months from the date of service. Medicaid: set by each state. Commercial payers: set by contract, often 90 to 180 days and sometimes shorter.

Miss the window and the denial usually can't be appealed. Know the limit for every payer you bill.

#timelyfiling #medicalbilling #claimdenials #revenuecycle #rcm #arcaller

2026-11-20.topic: Carousel "5 front-desk errors that cause denials" (4 slides)
2026-11-20.caption:
Many denials start at check-in, not in the billing office.

Name and date of birth mismatches, old member IDs, the wrong subscriber and plans that changed are all preventable with two habits: copy details from the card, and verify eligibility before the visit.

Save this and share it with your front-desk team.

#frontdesk #patientregistration #eligibilityverification #claimdenials #medicalbilling #practicemanagement

2026-11-21.caption:
Three code sets, three different jobs.

CPT says what was done. ICD-10-CM says why it was done. HCPCS Level II covers supplies, drugs, equipment and some services.

When the what and the why don't support each other, expect a medical-necessity denial.

#medicalcoding #cpt #icd10 #hcpcs #medicalbilling #cpc #codingstudent

2026-11-22.caption:
AR aging shows how long claims have gone unpaid: 0–30, 31–60, 61–90 and 90+ days.

The 90+ bucket is where money gets lost. Filing and appeal deadlines are closing in, and every week makes collection harder.

Work the oldest money first.

2026-11-24.caption:
Nearly 15% of claims sent to private payers are initially denied. More than half of those are paid in the end, but only after appeals that cost time and money. (Premier Inc. survey, 2024)

The cheapest denial is the one that never happens: clean data at registration, verified eligibility, accurate codes.

Three roles people mix up all the time.

Coders translate the visit into codes. Billers turn codes into clean claims. AR callers make sure those claims actually get paid.
